title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming parity across python/ts/go (v1.139.0)
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: This PR aligns the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs on a shared auth and retry model, brings streaming API parity and ergonomics fixes, and bumps SDK versions to v1.139.0. Motivation: customer feedback and internal consistency — we observed subtle differences in token refresh, retry fast-fail behavior, and streaming framing across SDKs which caused developer confusion and intermittent production regressions. What changed: unified auth flow (short-lived tokens + background refresh), central retry policy (idempotency-aware exponential backoff with jitter), streaming client parity (stream chunk framing and reconnect semantics), API ergonomics improvements (TS typings, Go context propagation, PY convenience helpers), and version bumps for all three SDKs. Checklist: - [x] Python: unify auth adapter, retry middleware, streaming client parity - [x] TypeScript: auth provider changes, unified retry strategy, improved stream typings - [x] Go: exported ergonomic helpers, context-aware streaming, retry wrapper - [x] Integration tests updated and passing (one flaky test rerun) - [x] Release notes drafted and approved Related: ENG-8421 (auth/retries audit), ENG-8473 (streaming parity work), SUP-1284 (customer incident impacting streaming reconnects). Notes: Kept changes backward-compatible where possible; old auth constructor remains but emits deprecation warning. Streaming reconnection uses an exponential reconnect cap of 30s; we added a server-side-compatible sentinel frame for drain detection. See commits for more context.
commits: feat(python): add AuthAdapter with background refresh and retry middleware
feat(ts): unified RetryStrategy + stream framing fixes
feat(go): context-aware streaming client and ergonomic helpers
test: add cross-sdk streaming integration tests
chore: bump versions to v1.139.0 for python/ts/go
fix: adjust TLS socket handling in ts stream client to avoid ulimit issues
